changelog: Adds Orca Observatory, an observability dashboard for the engine that lives inside the Jellyfin admin interface (Dashboard - Orca Observatory). It answers the questions the server log could not: which home row is the bottleneck, why a TMDB call failed, why a trailer is missing, why a title was recommended, and what the engine is doing right now. Eleven pages cover overview and engine health, per-row performance, metadata, the trailer resolver, the recommendation pipeline with per-pick score breakdowns, cache hit rates, a live log stream with full stack traces, a timeline of engine activity, and users. Behind it, every outbound call to TMDB, Sonarr, Radarr, Jellyseerr and the LLM is now timed and its failures recorded with status codes and exception detail, rather than collapsing into a bare counter; cache hits and misses, background maintenance ticks, and the previously invisible profile recompute backlog are all reported. IMPORTANT - administrative endpoints now require an authenticated Jellyfin administrator and return 403 otherwise. This covers all Admin and Observatory routes, the maintenance operations (catalog resync, reconcile, purge, TMDB and provider enrichment, global discovery pull, sweep, content-warning enrichment, community-rating recompute) and the operator diagnostics (trailer diagnostics, discovery runs and source stats); previously every one of these was reachable anonymously, including the endpoint that wipes all counters. Client-facing routes are unchanged. Also fixes a real defect: the plugin applied a cache size limit to Jellyfin's shared memory cache rather than its own, which could make unrelated server code throw when caching entries without a declared size. The engine now owns a private cache.
